findings.explanation: The CIM Authentication model describes login and authentication activity (user, src, dest, action). Wi-Fi presence and dwell events from Cisco Spaces are not authentication events, so the model does not fit the signal. The matching `dataModelAcceleration` advice ('Enable for Authentication') would waste acceleration on an unrelated dataset.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `cimModels` to an empty list and set `dataModelAcceleration` to 'Not applicable'. No CIM model covers location dwell analytics.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1352 is 'App for Cisco Network Data' (cisco_ios), a dashboard app for IOS, NX-OS and WLC data. It is not a Cisco Security add-on and plays no part in Cisco Spaces dwell analytics.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 1352 reference along with the generic Cisco Security support link. Cite the Cisco Spaces Firehose event-type and sample-event documentation instead.

findings.explanation: The text names no index, sourcetype or fields, while the search assumes `sourcetype=cisco:spaces:location` with flat `entryTime`, `exitTime`, `zoneName`, `building` and `floor`. Firehose DEVICE_PRESENCE nests its data under `devicePresence`. The fields are `entryTimestamp` and `exitTimestamp` (epoch milliseconds, exit 0 until the visit ends) and `visitDurationMinutes`, with a location hierarchy (`location.name`, `location.parent.name`, `floorNumber`) rather than a zoneName.
findings.quote: Cisco Spaces Firehose API (DEVICE_LOCATION_UPDATE, DEVICE_PRESENCE events — entry, exit, dwell)
findings.suggested_fix: List the index, the sourcetype the Spaces Add-On actually writes (verify it; third-party setup notes indicate `cisco:spaces:firehose`), and the real JSON paths: `devicePresence.presenceEventType`, `devicePresence.visitDurationMinutes`, `devicePresence.entryTimestamp`/`exitTimestamp` (ms) and `devicePresence.location.*`. State that dwell is only complete on DEVICE_EXIT_EVENT records.

findings.explanation: The title and `visualization` (Sankey of movement flows between zones) promise flow analysis. The search only computes dwell statistics per zone from DEVICE_PRESENCE and never reads DEVICE_LOCATION_UPDATE or sequences zones per device. The `implementation` waves at the flow half in one sentence without a method.
findings.quote: Build movement flow analysis by sequencing location updates per device MAC.
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe the flow method concretely (DEVICE_LOCATION_UPDATE per deviceId, sorted by time, with streamstats to get the previous zone and then counts of zone-to-zone transitions; compare sibling UC-15.3.38) or limit the text and visualization to dwell time per location.

findings.explanation: Wi-Fi device presence covers all devices, employees included, so 'visitor' dwell is really device dwell, and patient-flow claims go beyond what MAC-level presence supports. The UC also omits the privacy and consent constraints of tracking device MACs.
findings.quote: For healthcare, it tracks patient flow through departments to reduce wait times.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the output as device dwell per location, mention filtering by `visitClassification`/`deviceClassification` or SSID to approximate visitors, and add a note on privacy (MAC hashing, retention, consent).

findings.explanation: The scenarios contain no real dwell-time distortions. Real ones are fixed or stationary devices (printers, kiosks, laptops left on desks) inflating max dwell, MAC randomisation splitting a visit into several, and the inactivity/exit timeouts stretching dwell beyond actual presence.
findings.quote: **Synthetic probe on `zoneName`, `building`, `floor`** — Health checks in `cisco_spaces` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List those causes and suggest excluding device types or manufacturers associated with fixed infrastructure, or capping dwell at a plausible maximum.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `exitTime`, `entryTime`, `zoneName`, `building` and `floor` are not fields in Firehose DEVICE_PRESENCE. The real paths are `devicePresence.entryTimestamp`/`exitTimestamp` in epoch milliseconds, so `/60` yields thousandths of minutes rather than minutes, plus `devicePresence.visitDurationMinutes` and `devicePresence.location.*` (https://developer.cisco.com/docs/cisco-spaces-firehose/sample-events/). Entry events have `exitTimestamp=0`, which yields negative dwell. As written, the search returns nothing or wrong values.
An Authentication data-model count by user, action and src has nothing to do with dwell time or movement flow.

summary: The goal (dwell time per zone from Cisco Spaces presence events) is reasonable. However, the UC maps to the CIM Authentication model, cites a Cisco networking app under a wrong name, and its search uses field names and units that do not match Firehose DEVICE_PRESENCE events. The 'movement flow' half of the title is never implemented, and the detailed implementation carries pasted boilerplate.
